headline: ROGUE learns to fight at range
lede: The Dungeons of Doom got their away-game back: f throws arrows you can walk back and salvage, and finds charged staves that crackle lightning down corridors — the 1980 original's ranged shelf, restored whole, rings and all the fine print still honestly missing.

notes.text: Staves `/` generate with 3–9 charges — lightning, fire, cold, striking — spend one per zap and crumble to dust with the last.
Arrows arrive as counted quivers on the original's single weapon glyph; one leaves the pack per throw, a miss drops it on the flight line to pick back up, and quivers stack into bigger piles.
Every shot roll rides the state-carried entropy stream, so a pinned seed still replays arrow-for-arrow — and the WATCH pilot deliberately keeps its proven melee law.

The never-dry shelf walked past a stuck ADVENTURE kick (every gap was QA-owned by paraphrase) to ROGUE, whose oldest unowned gap was this one — item 5 of #3489 (parseGaps counting Restored bullets) explains the phantom.

look.text: Shoot the kestrel before it reaches you — f, then a direction.
